messages:
Sam W: FYI ran a full nsys + perfetto pass on the INT8/FP8 rollout. Throughput drops after KV cache warms (~30–40 tokens) and we see repeated host memcpy spikes between attention kernels. trace: https://perfetto.redwood/reports/abc123 :thinking_face:
PerfBot: nsys upload complete: https://nsys.redwood/traces/1862345678 :white_check_mark:
Maya R: can you paste the nsys command + the small kernel timeline snippet? want to see exact kernel names and ordering.
Sam W: cmd i used:
```bash
nsys profile --output trace_1862345678 --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt \
  --sample=none --capture-range=cudaAPI,start,end --stats=true \
  --target-args "--model my-quantized-model --seq-len 128 --batch 4"
```
kernel timeline (condensed):
```
contrib_attn_int8_kernel       180us
kv_copy_async                  120us (device->host)
dequant_fusion_kernel          340us
mixed_fp8_gemm                 210us
kv_apply_host_repack           90us
```
Andrew L: that kv_copy_async + dequant_fusion combo screams host fallback. looks like kernel_picker picks the mixed_fp8 path for long seqs and then we dequant on host. fallback triggers when selected GEMM doesn't support the sequence shape.
Maya R: do we have the picker rule? which threshold decides fp8 vs int8?
Sam W: snippet from kernel_picker.py:
```py
# simplified
if seq_len > 64 or batch_tokens > 8192:
    choose_mixed_fp8 = True
else:
    choose_int8 = True
```
Sam W: so at 128 tokens we take the mixed_fp8 path. but our mixed_fp8 path currently does a device->host dequant step for historic reasons (compat with older kernels). that's the hostcopy spike.
Andrew L: two levers: lower the threshold so we use int8 kernels for more shapes, or implement fused device-side dequant so no host roundtrip. tradeoffs: int8 may increase generation perplexity by ~0.4–0.9% for some models; fused-dequant keeps accuracy but needs kernel work.
Maya R: do we have quick perf numbers if we force int8 for seq=128?
Sam W: microbench numbers (A100, batch=4):
- current mixed_fp8 (fallback host dequant): throughput 320 tokens/s, dequant+hostcopy overhead ~45%
- force int8: throughput 480 tokens/s, ppl delta +0.6% on val set
- fused-device-dequant prototype: throughput 680 tokens/s, ppl delta +0.2%
Maya R: wow fused looks great. how stable is the prototype?
Sam W: prototype is a local hack, not yet memory-safe for kv>64k. need tests for correctness on long context. also need to offload fewer CPU copies.
Andrew L: other hypothesis: batching heuristics cause more simultaneous kv copies when many small batches align. check scheduler's pack_window and prefer_local_batch thresholds. if packs coalesce badly we might amplify hostcopy spikes.
Sam W: confirmed: when pack_window=8 and many 1-token requests hit, KV copy concurrency jumps. reduced pack_window to 4 in sandbox and hostcopy spikes dropped ~30%.
CI-bot: created ticket INF-2219: "kernel fallback: fused-dequant + batching heuristics" with links to traces: https://nsys.redwood/traces/1862345678 and perfetto report.
Maya R: action items: 1) Sam to land microbench harness (seq=[32,64,128,256], batch=[1,4,8]) and run across int8/fused/fp8; 2) Andrew to prototype fused-device-dequant memory-safety and KV edge cases; 3) DevEx to add kernel-fallback metric to Console (count of host-dequant fallbacks / minute).
Sam W: will open PR for harness + baseline numbers, and push prototype branch for fused kernel. PR link: https://git.redwood/r/sam/fused-deq (draft).
Maya R: also add an eval run to measure ppl/perf tradeoff for the top 3 production models. want concrete numbers before any global rollback.
Andrew L: i'll help with correctness tests and microbench CI. if fused holds, we can raise the fp8 threshold back up and keep perf/accuracy.
Sam W: thanks. I'll post updates in this thread as traces and CI runs finish. :thumbsup:
